descriptors.definition: The stand-alone selling price is established at contract inception as the specific price at which an entity sells promised goods or services separately to customers. Observable standalone pricing serves as the primary evidence, while unobservable prices must be estimated to satisfy transaction allocation objectives.
inclusion: Determining standalone prices at contract inception
Using observable standalone prices
Estimating unobservable prices
exclusion: Updating standalone prices for intervening market changes without contract modification
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from transaction price allocation changes driven by subsequent variable events

descriptors.definition: Subsequent changes in the transaction price are allocated to performance obligations on the same basis as established at contract inception without updating historical stand-alone selling prices. Amounts tied to fully satisfied performance obligations are recognized immediately as revenue adjustments in the period of change.
inclusion: Allocating post-inception price changes on original bases
Adjusting revenue for satisfied obligations when prices change
exclusion: Reallocating transaction prices to reflect updated stand-alone selling prices
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from initial transaction price determination at contract inception

descriptors.definition: Revenue is recognized when an entity fulfills a performance obligation by transferring promised assets or services to a customer. The decisive determinant for this transfer is whether the customer acquires control over the underlying asset.
inclusion: Evaluating control transfer criteria at contract inception
Recognizing revenue upon asset transfer
exclusion: Recognizing revenue prior to the customer acquiring control
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from contract identification and transaction price steps

descriptors.definition: Control of an asset denotes the customer's present ability to direct its use and obtain substantially all remaining benefits while preventing other entities from doing so. Indicators such as legal title, physical possession, and present payment rights help identify when this transfer occurs.
inclusion: Evaluating customer ability to direct asset use
Assessing cash flow generation and benefit extraction
Reviewing transfer indicators like payment rights and legal title
exclusion: Treating mere physical possession without control indicators as a transfer
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from physical delivery arrangements that lack customer control

descriptors.concept_name: Transfer of Control Over a Period of Time
descriptors.definition: An entity transfers control and recognizes revenue over time if the customer simultaneously receives and consumes benefits, creates or enhances an asset controlled by the customer, or leaves the entity without an alternative use asset paired with an enforceable payment right. Routine recurring services typically meet the criteria where benefits are simultaneously received and consumed.
inclusion: Recognizing revenue when customers simultaneously receive and consume benefits
Evaluating asset creation under customer control
exclusion: Recognizing revenue at a point in time when none of the over-time criteria are met
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from point-in-time revenue recognition models

descriptors.definition: A repurchase agreement involves selling an asset while promising or holding an option to repurchase the same or a substantially similar asset. Such transactions are accounted for as leases or financing arrangements rather than outright sales if the customer is restricted from directing the asset's use.
inclusion: Evaluating forward and call option arrangements
Classifying repurchases below selling price as leases
Classifying repurchases at or above selling price as financing arrangements
exclusion: Recognizing immediate absolute sales when entity repurchase commitments exist
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard unconditional sales of goods

descriptors.definition: Bill-and-hold arrangements allow billing for a product while the entity retains physical possession until a future date. Revenue is recognized when the customer obtains control, provided substantive reasons exist, items are separately identified as belonging to the customer, products are ready for transfer, and the entity cannot redirect the items.
inclusion: Recognizing revenue when control transfers despite retained physical possession
Segregating custodial service performance obligations
exclusion: Recognizing revenue where goods are unidentifiable or subject to entity redirection
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard delivery-based revenue recognition

descriptors.definition: Licences of intellectual property are evaluated to determine whether the promise provides a right to access intellectual property over time or a right to use it as it exists at a point in time. Access rights result from ongoing entity activities that significantly affect the intellectual property, exposing the customer to positive or negative changes.
inclusion: Evaluating licences of software, technology, media, and franchises
Recognizing access-right licence revenue over time
exclusion: Treating static static-use licences as performance obligations satisfied over time

descriptors.definition: Contract costs comprise incremental expenses incurred to obtain contracts and direct costs necessary to fulfill performance obligations. Incremental costs to obtain and fulfill contracts expected to be recovered are capitalized as assets and systematically amortized.
inclusion: Capitalizing incremental contract acquisition costs
Capitalizing direct contract fulfilment costs
exclusion: Expensing non-incremental acquisition costs like routine proposal travel or negotiation legal fees
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished between contract acquisition expenses and contract fulfilment resources

descriptors.definition: Incremental costs incurred to obtain a contract with a customer that would not have been incurred otherwise are capitalized as assets when expected to be recovered. Costs that would have been incurred regardless of whether the contract was secured must be expensed as incurred.
inclusion: Capitalizing commissions paid explicitly and solely upon successful contract signing
Applying the practical expedient to expense short-amortisation assets
exclusion: Capitalizing routine sales salaries, pitch travel expenses, or drafting legal fees
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from general marketing and proposal expenses incurred regardless of contract outcome

descriptors.definition: Costs incurred to fulfill a contract that fall outside other accounting standards are recognized as assets if they relate directly to a contract, generate or enhance resources for future satisfaction, and are expected to be recovered. General administrative expenses and wasted resource costs must be expensed as incurred.
inclusion: Recognizing assets for direct labour and materials tied to specific contracts
Including supervision and subcontractor costs
exclusion: Capitalizing general administrative overhead or costs of wasted materials
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from contract acquisition costs and costs governed by inventories or property standards

descriptors.definition: Capitalized contract costs are amortized systematically in a manner consistent with the transfer pattern of the related goods or services. Impairment losses are recognized in earnings when carrying amounts exceed remaining expected consideration net of direct costs.
inclusion: Systematic amortisation of capitalized contract assets
Recognizing and reversing contract cost impairments
exclusion: Applying variable consideration constraints when calculating expected remaining consideration for impairment
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from standard tangible asset depreciation models
